title: MCP: edit and delete a document tool (ChangeTool, DeleteTool)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
**What's missing:** a document tool can be added over MCP (`add_tool`), but it can't be edited or deleted. The tool editor's commands are `ChangeTool` (replace the definition, so ops on the tool turn stale) and `DeleteTool` (remove it; undo restores its number and body), both in `crates/app/src/commands/tool.rs`. A headless agent that needs a longer stickout, a different flute count or another rpm has to add a second tool under a new name and re-point every op with `set_tool`. A tool added by mistake can only go by `undo`.

**Neighbour that works:** `edit_operation { name, params }` applies a JSON merge patch over an op's fields, refuses an unknown field by name, and runs `EditOperationParams` (`crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs`).

**Done means:**
- `edit_tool { name, definition }` applies a JSON merge patch over the tool's `get_job` definition, refuses an unknown field by name, and runs `ChangeTool` through `env.history`, one undo step. The command's own refusals come back as tool errors: non-finite or non-positive numbers, a retype the tool law refuses for an op using the tool, a body that no longer fits.
- `delete_tool { name }` runs `DeleteTool`, one undo step. The reply names any operations that still use the tool.
- In-process JSON-RPC tests pin both: an edit makes the op stale, undo restores it, and the refusals are named. They also cover what verify and post do once a used tool is gone.

Labels per AGENTS.md for an agent-filed issue: `enhancement`, `P2`, `area:ui`, `source:agent` (this account can't set labels).
